questions.question: What distinguishes a multimodal system from an API that merely accepts several file types?
options: It defines how evidence is aligned, fused, and handled when a modality is missing or contradictory
It always converts every input into plain text before inference
It requires every modality to have the same number of tokens
It guarantees that adding a modality improves accuracy
questions.explanation: The system contract includes alignment, fusion, contribution, trust, and degraded-input behavior; multiple upload fields alone do not provide those guarantees.

questions.question: Which fusion boundary best fits cross-modal catalog retrieval when product images can be indexed before queries arrive?
options: A shared-space dual encoder
Token-level cross-attention for every stored image
A late vote over unrelated class labels
A text-only classifier
questions.explanation: Independent encoders let the catalog image embeddings be precomputed while text queries are embedded online and compared in the shared space.

questions.question: Why can token-level cross-attention cost grow quickly as visual and language sequences get longer?
options: Cross-modal token pairs grow with the product of the two sequence lengths
Every token must be written to object storage
The model trains a new encoder for every request
Late fusion duplicates the complete dataset
questions.explanation: A visual sequence of V tokens and a language sequence of L tokens can create V x L cross-modal comparisons in an attention layer.

questions.question: A slide deck is older than the transcript it is paired with. What is the safest first system response?
options: Mark the slides stale, exclude or limit their authority, and expose the degraded state
Treat both inputs as aligned because each file parsed successfully
Replace the transcript with the slide text
Increase the model temperature
questions.explanation: Parsing success does not prove temporal alignment. The system must preserve timestamps and make stale evidence explicit.

questions.question: What evaluation most directly shows whether fusion adds useful evidence?
options: Compare the fused model with each unimodal baseline and with missing, stale, and conflicting modality slices
Report only one aggregate benchmark score
Measure the model file size
Count the number of supported media types
questions.explanation: Unimodal baselines expose modality contribution, while degraded slices reveal whether the system remains safe when the input contract is violated.

questions.question: An image contains text telling the model to override tool policy. How should the application treat it?
options: As untrusted content evidence that cannot grant new instruction or tool authority
As a higher-priority system instruction because it is inside an image
As safe once the image decoder succeeds
As a reason to skip audit logging
questions.explanation: Content extracted from media remains untrusted input. Tool and policy authority must come from the application boundary, not from a modality.
